question: What was the original scope of Regulation 22 in the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013, and how did the 2020 amendment fundamentally change its coverage?
reference_answer: The original Regulation 22 (2013) was titled 'Segregation of execution services' and applied only to investment advisers that are banks, NBFCs, and body corporates which also provide distribution or execution services. Such entities could continue offering distribution services alongside advice provided they maintained operational segregation, ensured clients were not obligated to avail distribution services, maintained arms-length relationships, and ensured fees were paid directly to service providers. Individual investment advisers were not explicitly covered. The SEBI (Investment Advisers) (Amendment) Regulations, 2020 (w.e.f. 30-09-2020) completely substituted Regulation 22 — retitling it 'Client level segregation of advisory and distribution activities.' The 2020 version imposed a complete prohibition on individual investment advisers (and their families) from providing distribution services, and replaced the prior operational-segregation approach for non-individual entities with a stricter client-level segregation at the group level.

However, with the 2020 amendment, Regulation 22 was made more stringent, requiring individual investment advisers (IAs) to cease providing distribution services and non-individual IAs to maintain client-level segregation at the group level [SEBI (IA) (Amendment) Regulations, 2020, w.e.f. 30-09-2020 / para 1]. The amendment also introduced a new requirement for IAs to maintain a segregated investment advisory services fund [SEBI (IA) (Amendment) Regulations, 2020, w.e.f. 30-09-2020 / para 1].

The 2020 amendment replaced this with two separate requirements: (i) at least one key personnel must hold a relevant SEBI-specified certification (not a minimum years-of-experience requirement), and (ii) at least one key personnel must hold a finance-related professional qualification or CFA Charter. question: Under SEBI IA Regulations, 2013, if an investment adviser advised clients to buy a stock on a certain date but subsequently believes the situation has changed within 10 days, can the adviser immediately sell the same stock from its own account?
reference_answer: No, not immediately. Under Regulation 15(7), an investment adviser is prohibited from entering transactions on its own account contrary to client advice for 15 days from the day of advice. Even if the situation has changed within those 15 days, the adviser cannot act immediately — it must first give a revised assessment to clients at least 24 hours in advance before entering the contrary own-account transaction. So the adviser must provide the revised assessment and then wait at least 24 hours before selling from its own account.
